title: Sarga Nine — verses 1–95
html:
Title of the sarga: none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
Metre: svāgatā (11 syllables per pada: —⏑— ⏑⏑⏑ —⏑⏑ ——); verse 94 — praharṣiṇī; verse 95 — mandākrāntā.
Total verses: 95.

Contents of the passage: Srivasa's account of Krishna's pastimes with the gopis — the walk in the forest, the bathing in the Yamuna, the entry into the jewelled pavilion. - 1 — Srivasa begins his account (continuing 8.60–63). - 2–20 — the gopis enter the forest with Krishna: lightning beside a cloud; their first shyness yields to Manmatha; gestures and gaits; bees alight on the creepers of their bodies; the gopis walk embracing Krishna. - 21–31 — the Lakshmi of the forest brings gifts; the friends tease a proud one (kulaka 22–26: the mādhavī and the jasmine tormented by bees); a gopi embraces a creeper as a friend; "the cuckoo calls 'kuhū' — it is darkness you desire". - 32–47 — gathering flowers: Krishna is adorned with a flower, lifts the gopis to the high branches, calls Radha lotus-faced (34); a bee on Krishna; reproaches to the "bee" (kulaka 37–39); "there is a bower!"; balls of flowers; coaxing the proud one. - 48–50 — Krishna turns to another; the gopis are bathed in perspiration from the forest play. - 51–78 — the bathing in the Yamuna: splashing, the "water drum", the śapharī fish, lotuses and stalks hold back the garments; the washed-off colours and ornaments are gifts to the Yamuna; wet braids and garments. - 79–93 — a kulaka of fifteen verses: the jewelled pavilion (walls like mirrors, moonstones and sunstones, emerald "grass", ruby "pomegranates", a crystal pond). - 94–95 — the singing of the birds; the wish-fulfilling creepers perform nīrājana over the gopis with cries of "Victory!"

Verse 1

इत्थमुद्भटसुखाम्बुधिमग्नं
गौरचन्द्रमथ यथा सोऽभिजगाद ।
श्रूयतां प्रभुवर स्वविहारं
प्राक्कृतं स्वयमहं कथयामि ॥१॥

ittham udbhaṭa-sukhāmbudhi-magnaṁ
gauracandram atha yathā so 'bhijagāda |
śrūyatāṁ prabhu-vara sva-vihāraṁ
prāk-kṛtaṁ svayam ahaṁ kathayāmi ||1||

ittham — thus; udbhaṭa — of mighty; sukha — happiness; ambudhi — in the ocean; magnam — immersed; gauracandram — to Gaurachandra; atha — then; yathā (?) — (as); saḥ — he (Srivasa); abhijagāda — said; śrūyatām — let it be heard; prabhu — of lords; vara — O best; sva — Your own; vihāram — pastime; prāk — formerly; kṛtam — performed; svayam — myself; aham — I; kathayāmi — shall tell.

1Then he said to Gaurachandra, thus immersed in an ocean of mighty happiness: "Listen, O best of lords: I myself shall tell [You] of Your own pastimes, performed of old."

Note. The second pada in the edition (गौरचन्द्रमथ यथा सोऽभिजगाद) has 13 syllables instead of 11; without yathā (gauracandram atha so 'bhijagāda) the svāgatā metre is restored exactly, so yathā is probably an interpolation or a misprint (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 2

वीक्ष्य तद्वदनमनिर्वचनीयं
रम्यरम्यमपि वल्गुमनोभिः ।
श्रेयसा सह विलासवतीभिः
स्वाङ्गवल्लिभिरकारि विचित्रम् ॥२॥

vīkṣya tad-vadanam anirvacanīyaṁ
ramya-ramyam api valgu-manobhiḥ |
śreyasā [preyasā] saha vilāsavatībhiḥ
svāṅga-vallibhir akāri vicitram ||2||

vīkṣya — having seen; tat — His; vadanam — face; anirvacanīyam — indescribable; ramya-ramyam — the most charming of the charming; api — and; valgu — tender; manobhiḥ — with hearts; preyasā — with the beloved; saha — together; vilāsavatībhiḥ — by the playful [maidens]; sva — of their own; aṅga — limbs; vallibhiḥ — with the creepers; akāri — was made; vicitram — a wonder.

2Seeing His indescribable face, the most charming of all that is charming, the playful [maidens], tender-hearted, wrought wonders with the creepers of their limbs together with their beloved.

Note. The edition has श्रेयसा ("with the good"); cf. preyasā in verse 3: we read preyasā (?). The first pada has 12 syllables instead of 11; with tan-mukham in place of tad-vadanam the svāgatā metre is exact — perhaps a gloss has displaced the original word (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 3

प्रेयसा सह नवीनतमाल-
श्यामलेन विपिनं प्रविशन्तः ।
तत्पुरो नवघनेन विलासं
विद्युतां दधुरमूर्व्रजवध्वः ॥३॥

preyasā saha navīna-tamāla-
śyāmalena vipinaṁ praviśantaḥ [praviśantyaḥ] |
tat-puro nava-ghanena vilāsaṁ
vidyutāṁ dadhur amūr vraja-vadhvaḥ ||3||

preyasā — with the beloved; saha — together; navīna — young; tamāla — [as] a tamala tree; śyāmalena — dark; vipinam — the forest; praviśantyaḥ — entering; tat — Him; puraḥ — before; nava — new; ghanena — with a cloud; vilāsam — the play; vidyutām — of lightnings; dadhuḥ — displayed; amūḥ — these; vraja — of Vraja; vadhvaḥ — the young women.

3Entering the forest together with their beloved, dark as a young tamala tree, these young women of Vraja displayed before Him the play of lightnings with a new rain cloud.

Note. The edition has praviśantaḥ, a masculine form with a feminine subject; the sense requires praviśantyaḥ (the metre is unchanged) (?). The golden gopis before Krishna, dark as a cloud, are like lightning on a cloud. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 4

रामणीयकमवेक्ष्य रमण्यो
मानसेन मनसिजेन लसन्त्यः ।
चेष्टया रुचिरयालसभाजो
भाविताः समभवन्नधिनाथम् ॥४॥

rāmaṇīyakam avekṣya ramaṇyo
mānasena manasijena lasantyaḥ |
ceṣṭayā rucirayālasa-bhājo
bhāvitāḥ samabhavann adhinātham ||4||

rāmaṇīyakam — the loveliness; avekṣya — having beheld; ramaṇyaḥ — the beautiful women; mānasena — heartfelt; manasijena — with love; lasantyaḥ — shining; ceṣṭayā — with movement; rucirayā — charming; ālasa — languor; bhājaḥ — possessing; bhāvitāḥ — filled with feeling; samabhavan — became; adhinātham — towards their master.

4Beholding His loveliness, the beautiful women shone with love born in the heart; charming in their movements, full of languor, they became wholly filled with feeling for their master.

Note. Rucirayālasa- = rucirayā (agreeing with ceṣṭayā) + ālasa. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 5

साभिलासमथ भाववतीनां
कृष्णचन्द्रमभिमुग्धवधूनाम् ।
साध्वसं प्रथमजं तिरयित्वा
मन्मथेन हृदये समुदासे ॥५॥

sābhilāṣam atha bhāvavatīnāṁ
kṛṣṇacandram abhi mugdha-vadhūnām |
sādhvasaṁ prathamajaṁ tirayitvā
manmathena hṛdaye samudāse ||5||

sa — with; abhilāṣam — longing; atha — then; bhāvavatīnām — full of feeling; kṛṣṇacandram — Krishnachandra; abhi — towards; mugdha — innocent; vadhūnām — of the young women; sādhvasam — shyness; prathama — of the first [meeting]; jam — born; tirayitvā — having dispelled; manmathena — by Manmatha; hṛdaye — in the heart; samudāse — it was risen (he arose).

5Then, in the hearts of the innocent young women, full of feeling and longing for Krishnachandra, Manmatha arose, dispelling the shyness born of the first [meeting].

Note. The edition has साभिलास for the usual sābhilāṣa. Samudāse is an impersonal passive perfect (bhāve prayoga): "it was risen by Manmatha", that is, Manmatha arose.

Verse 6

अंशुकं शिथिलितं द्रढयित्वा
बिभ्रती सचकितत्रपमेका ।
सस्मितप्रियसखीजनपार्श्वे
लीलया लघु चलन्त्यभिरेजे ॥६॥

aṁśukaṁ śithilitaṁ draḍhayitvā
bibhratī sa-cakita-trapam ekā |
sa-smita-priya-sakhī-jana-pārśve
līlayā laghu calanty abhireje ||6||

aṁśukam — the garment; śithilitam — loosened; draḍhayitvā — having tightened; bibhratī — holding; sa — with; cakita — alarm; trapam — [and] shame; ekā — one; sa — with; smita — smiles; priya — of dear; sakhī — friends; jana — of the company; pārśve — to the side; līlayā — playfully; laghu — lightly; calantī — moving; abhireje — shone.

6One, startled and abashed, tightened her loosened garment and, holding it, moved lightly and playfully to the side of her dear, smiling friends — and she shone.

Verse 7

कापि मन्दमयता परिवृत्ते
मारुतेन कुचयुग्मकचेले ।
सम्भ्रमात् प्रियसखीजनमुच्चै-
रालिलिङ्ग परिपश्यति कृष्णे ॥७॥

kāpi mandam ayatā parivṛtte
mārutena kuca-yugma-kacele |
sambhramāt priya-sakhī-janam uccair
āliliṅga paripaśyati kṛṣṇe ||7||

kā api — a certain [maiden]; mandam — gently; ayatā — blowing; parivṛtte — when [it] was turned aside; mārutena — by the breeze; kuca — of the breasts; yugma — of the pair; kacele — the covering; sambhramāt — in confusion; priya — dear; sakhī — friend; janam — from the circle; uccaiḥ — tightly; āliliṅga — embraced; paripaśyati — while looking on; kṛṣṇe — Krishna.

7When the gently blowing breeze turned aside the covering of another's bosom while Krishna looked on, she in confusion tightly embraced a dear friend.

Note. Kacela is a rare word, apparently a covering for the bosom or a bodice; possibly a corruption. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 8

उन्नमय्य भुजयुग्ममथान्या
पीवरस्तनयुगोन्नमनेन ।
साङ्गभङ्गमलसेन लसन्ती
जृम्भतेस्म पुरतो दयितस्य ॥८॥

unnamayya bhuja-yugmam athānyā
pīvara-stana-yugonnamanena |
sāṅga-bhaṅgam alasena lasantī
jṛmbhate sma purato dayitasya ||8||

unnamayya — having raised; bhuja — of arms; yugmam — the pair; atha — and; anyā — another; pīvara — full; stana — of breasts; yuga — of the pair; unnamanena — with the lifting; sa — with; aṅga — of the body; bhaṅgam — a bending; alasena — languidly; lasantī — shining; jṛmbhate sma — stretched with a yawn; purataḥ — before; dayitasya — the beloved.

8And another, raising both her arms, so that her full bosom was lifted, and languidly bending her whole body, stretched with a yawn before her beloved, radiant.

Verse 9

पीवरोरसिजकुड्मलकान्तां
पाणिधूतनवपल्लवकान्तिम् ।
प्रोज्झ्य काननलतां वरनारी-
देहवल्लिमभजन्मधुपौघः ॥९॥

pīvarorasija-kuḍmala-kāntāṁ
pāṇi-dhūta-nava-pallava-kāntim |
projjhya kānana-latāṁ vara-nārī-
deha-vallim abhajan madhupaughaḥ ||9||

pīvara — full; urasija — of breasts; kuḍmala — with the buds; kāntām — lovely; pāṇi — by the hands; dhūta — put to shame; nava — of young; pallava — shoots; kāntim — [whose] beauty; projjhya — having abandoned; kānana — of the forest; latām — the creeper; vara — of a beautiful; nārī — woman; deha — of the body; vallim — the creeper; abhajat — resorted to; madhupa — of bees; oghaḥ — a swarm.

9Abandoning the forest creeper, a swarm of bees resorted to the creeper of the body of a beautiful maiden — lovely with the buds of her full bosom, her hands putting to shame the beauty of young shoots.

Note. In the edition the lines are wrongly divided (प्रोज्झ्य काननलतां — / वरनारी देहवल्लि…): by the metre, vara-nārī belongs to the third pada.

Verse 10

सुभ्रुवां तनुलतासु लतानां
श्रीरियं सपरितोषमभूत् किम् ।
सर्वतः सपदि तासु यदेतन्-
मञ्जुगुञ्जदलिनां कुलमासीत् ॥१०॥

subhruvāṁ tanu-latāsu latānāṁ
śrīr iyaṁ sa-paritoṣam abhūt kim |
sarvataḥ sapadi tāsu yad etan
mañju-guñjad-alināṁ kulam āsīt ||10||

subhruvām — of the fair-browed; tanu — of the bodies; latāsu — into the creepers; latānām — of the creepers; śrīḥ — beauty; iyam — this; sa — with; paritoṣam — delight; abhūt — passed (came to dwell); kim — did not?; sarvataḥ — from all sides; sapadi — at once; tāsu — around them; yat — since; etat — this; mañju — sweetly; guñjat — humming; alinām — of bees; kulam — swarm; āsīt — appeared.

10Had not the beauty of the creepers joyfully passed into the creepers of the bodies of the fair-browed [maidens]? For at once, on all sides, this swarm of sweetly humming bees appeared around them.

Verse 11

एकयौष्ठपतनेऽमृतपत्वं
प्रेप्सुरुन्मदतरो मधुपायी ।
ओष्ठदंशनरतस्य सतोषं
प्रेयसः स्मरणतो न निरासे ॥११॥

ekayauṣṭha-patane 'mṛta-pa-tvaṁ
prepsur unmadataro madhu-pāyī |
oṣṭha-daṁśana-ratasya satoṣaṁ
preyasaḥ smaraṇato na nirāse ||11||

ekayā — by one; oṣṭha — on the lip; patane — on falling; amṛta — of nectar; pa — of a drinker; tvam — the state; prepsuḥ — desiring to obtain; unmadataraḥ — greatly intoxicated; madhu — honey; pāyī — drinking (the bee); oṣṭha — the lips; daṁśana — to biting; ratasya — given; satoṣam — gladly; preyasaḥ — of the beloved; smaraṇataḥ — from remembrance; na — not; nirāse — was driven away.

11A greatly intoxicated honey-drinking bee, longing to become a drinker of nectar, fell on the lip of one [maiden]; and she gladly did not drive it away, remembering her beloved, who is given to biting the lips.

Note. Amṛta-pa-tvam — "the state of a drinker of nectar" (amṛta-pa + -tva). Nirāse is an impersonal passive: "by one [maiden] there was no driving away".

Verse 12

मन्थरं मदनविह्वलहंसी-
लास्यशंसि मधुरक्रमरम्यम् ।
आदधुश्चरणपङ्कजरम्यं
सुभ्रुवोऽथ लघु तत्र विहर्तुम् ॥१२॥

mantharaṁ madana-vihvala-haṁsī-
lāsya-śaṁsi madhura-krama-ramyam |
ādadhuś caraṇa-paṅkaja-ramyaṁ
subhruvo 'tha laghu tatra vihartum ||12||

mantharam — slow; madana — by love; vihvala — overwhelmed; haṁsī — of a female swan; lāsya — the dance; śaṁsi — recalling; madhura — with sweet; krama — steps; ramyam — charming; ādadhuḥ — displayed; caraṇa — of the feet; paṅkaja — of the lotuses; ramyam — the loveliness; subhruvaḥ — the fair-browed; atha — then; laghu — lightly; tatra — there; vihartum — in order to play.

12Then, in order to play there, the fair-browed [maidens] displayed the loveliness of their lotus feet — a light, unhurried [gait], charming with its sweet steps, recalling the dance of a female swan overwhelmed by love.

Note. The syntax is unclear: the attributes mantharam … madhura-krama-ramyam imply "gait" (gatim), while the second ramyam is probably a noun, "loveliness". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 13

उल्लसन्मदनमन्थरपाद-
न्यासभाजि गमने रमणीनाम् ।
श्रोणिबिम्बकुचयोः परिणाहः
खेदयन्नपि बभूव सुखाय ॥१३॥

ullasan-madana-manthara-pāda-
nyāsa-bhāji gamane ramaṇīnām |
śroṇi-bimba-kucayoḥ pariṇāhaḥ
khedayann api babhūva sukhāya ||13||

ullasat — swelling; madana — by love; manthara — slowed; pāda — of the feet; nyāsa — placing; bhāji — having; gamane — in the gait; ramaṇīnām — of the beautiful women; śroṇi — of the hips; bimba — rounded; kucayoḥ — [and] of the breasts; pariṇāhaḥ — the fullness; khedayan — wearying; api — though; babhūva — became; sukhāya — for happiness.

13As the beautiful women walked, their steps slowed by swelling love, the fullness of their rounded hips and bosoms, though it wearied them, became a source of happiness.

Note. In the edition the lines are wrongly divided (…पादन्यास / भाजि…): the boundary of the padas falls inside the word pāda-nyāsa.

Verse 14

वीचिभङ्ग इव काञ्चनकाञ्ची-
कामडिण्डिमरवेण नितम्बः ।
सुभ्रुवां गमनविभ्रमभूषो
मन्दमन्दमलसेन ननर्त ॥१४॥

vīci-bhaṅga iva kāñcana-kāñcī-
kāma-ḍiṇḍima-raveṇa nitambaḥ |
subhruvāṁ gamana-vibhrama-bhūṣo
manda-mandam alasena nanarta ||14||

vīci — of a wave; bhaṅgaḥ — the curve; iva — like; kāñcana — golden; kāñcī — of the girdle; kāma — of Kama; ḍiṇḍima — of the drum; raveṇa — to the sound; nitambaḥ — the hips; subhruvām — of the fair-browed; gamana — of the gait; vibhrama — with the grace; bhūṣaḥ — adorned; manda-mandam — very slowly; alasena — languidly; nanarta — danced.

14To the sound of the golden girdle — the drum of Kama — the hips of the fair-browed [maidens], adorned with the grace of their gait, danced very slowly and languidly, like the curve of a wave.

Verse 15

कोमलं चरणपद्ममशक्तं
मास्म गा द्रुततरं मदिराक्षि ।
इत्यतीव विवशौ रुदतः किं
नूपुरौ प्रणयतो रमणीनाम् ॥१५॥

komalaṁ caraṇa-padmam aśaktaṁ
mā sma gā drutataraṁ madirākṣi |
ity atīva vivaśau rudataḥ kiṁ
nūpurau praṇayato ramaṇīnām ||15||

komalam — tender; caraṇa — of the foot; padmam — the lotus; aśaktam — without strength; mā sma gāḥ — do not go; drutataram — too quickly; madirā — intoxicating; akṣi — O [maiden] with eyes; iti — thus; atīva — utterly; vivaśau — helpless; rudataḥ — cry; kim — do [they] not?; nūpurau — the two anklets; praṇayataḥ — out of love; ramaṇīnām — of the beautiful women.

15"Tender is the lotus of your foot, it has no strength — do not go so quickly, O maiden with intoxicating eyes!" — is it not this that the anklets of the beautiful women, utterly helpless, cry out of love?

Verse 16

तत्तदङ्घ्रिकमलस्य विलासे
सस्पृहं कथयतीव महान्तम् ।
स्वानुरागमनुरागवतीनां
यावकैररुणिता वनभूमिः ॥१६॥

tat-tad-aṅghri-kamalasya vilāse
sa-spṛhaṁ kathayatīva mahāntam |
svānurāgam anurāgavatīnāṁ
yāvakair aruṇitā vana-bhūmiḥ ||16||

tat-tat — of each of them; aṅghri — of the feet; kamalasya — of the lotus; vilāse — for the play; sa — with; spṛham — longing; kathayati — tells; iva — as if; mahāntam — great; sva — its own; anurāgam — love (redness); anurāgavatīnām — of the loving [maidens]; yāvakaiḥ — with lac; aruṇitā — reddened; vana — of the forest; bhūmiḥ — the ground.

16Reddened with the lac from the feet of the loving [maidens], the forest ground seemed to tell longingly of its own great love for the play of the lotus feet of each of them.

Note. A play on words: anurāga means both "love" and "redness". The earth, reddened by yāvaka (the red lac for the feet), seems to confess its love.

Verse 17

कृष्णपृष्ठतटलग्नकुचाग्रा
तत्तदंसविलसद्भुजमूला ।
साचितद्वदनचुम्बितवक्त्रा
कापि तत्र रुरुचेऽनुचलन्ती ॥१७॥

kṛṣṇa-pṛṣṭha-taṭa-lagna-kucāgrā
tat-tad-aṁsa-vilasad-bhuja-mūlā |
sāci-tad-vadana-cumbita-vaktrā
kāpi tatra ruruce 'nucalantī ||17||

kṛṣṇa — of Krishna; pṛṣṭha — of the back; taṭa — to the slope; lagna — pressed; kuca — of the breasts; agrā — [whose] tips; tat-tat — now on one, now on the other of His; aṁsa — shoulders; vilasat — resting; bhuja — of the arms; mūlā — [whose] upper parts; sāci — turned sideways; tat — by His; vadana — face; cumbita — kissed; vaktrā — [whose] face; kā api — a certain [maiden]; tatra — there; ruruce — shone; anucalantī — following.

17There one [maiden] shone as she followed [Him], her bosom pressed to Krishna's back, her arms resting now on one, now on the other of His shoulders, her face kissed by His face as He turned it sideways.

Note. The compound sāci-tad-vadana-cumbita-vaktrā admits two readings: either Krishna, turning His face sideways, kisses her, or she, turning her face, kisses Him.

Verse 18

पृष्ठतः प्रियतमेन भुजाभ्यां

yatra daiva-vaśato madhupatvaṁ

90There the bee, in its folly, does not want a flower, taking it for a diamond, and clings to a diamond, taking it for a flower; so it was only by the will of fate that the bee ever attained the state of a "honey-drinker".

ekataḥ sphaṭika-pāṭala-gaurair

Verse 92

स्फाटिकं तटमभि प्रतिमग्नः
प्रोत्थितो द्युपतिरत्नतटान्ते ।
निर्भरं विलपति प्रतिकान्तां
यत्र चारुसरसीमभि कोकः ॥९२॥

sphāṭikaṁ taṭam abhi pratimagnaḥ
protthito dyupati-ratna-taṭānte |
nirbharaṁ vilapati pratikāntāṁ
yatra cāru-sarasīm abhi kokaḥ ||92||

sphāṭikam — crystal; taṭam abhi — at the bank; pratimagnaḥ — having dived; protthitaḥ — having emerged; dyu-pati — of the lord of the sky (the sun); ratna — of the gem; taṭa — of the bank; ante — at the edge; nirbharam — bitterly; vilapati — laments; prati — for; kāntām — [his] mate; yatra — where; cāru — lovely; sarasīm abhi — towards the lake; kokaḥ — the chakravaka.

92There a chakravaka, having dived at the crystal bank and emerged at the edge of the bank of sunstone, bitterly laments for his mate, turned towards the lovely lake.

Note. Dyupati-ratna ("the gem of the lord of the sky") is the sunstone (sūryakānta). The edition has prothito; the Gosvami edition (GGM) has protthito ("having emerged"), and so we read.

pañcadaśabhiḥ kulakam ||

93And the [maidens] with eyes pure as blue lotuses lightly, playfully entered that captivating, spacious, wondrous pavilion to adorn themselves, as moonlight [enters] an ocean of nectar. (A kulaka of fifteen verses.)

Note. Verses 79–93 form a kulaka, a single sentence: all the subordinate clauses with "where" (yatra) refer to the word ālayam ("pavilion").

śrīmadbhiḥ — by splendid; parabhṛta — cuckoos; barhi — peacocks; kīra — parrots; haṁsaiḥ — [and] swans; sat — by fine; pārāvata — turtle-doves; madhupa — of bees; āvalī — swarms; kapotaiḥ — [and] pigeons; anyonya — mutually; sva — their own [voices]; parivardhataḥ — from increasing; api — and; apūrvam — unprecedented; sambheje — attained; śravaṇa — for the ears; rasāyanatvam — the quality of an elixir; uccaiḥ — in the highest degree.

Note. The metre is praharṣiṇī. The subject of sambheje is not named; by the sense it is the "pavilion" of verse 93 (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 95

उद्गच्छन्तीष्वथ वरवधूष्वालयान्तेषु जाता
नानापुष्पैः सुरभिमधुरैः कल्पवल्ल्यः समन्तात् ।

udgacchantīṣv atha vara-vadhūṣv ālayānteṣu jātā
nānā-puṣpaiḥ surabhi-madhuraiḥ kalpa-vallyaḥ samantāt |
cakrur nīrājanam iva muhuḥ kūjitaiḥ kokilānāṁ

udgacchantīṣu — as [they] went up; atha — then; vara — lovely; vadhūṣu — the young women; ālaya — of the pavilion; anteṣu — within; jātāḥ — grown; nānā — with various; puṣpaiḥ — flowers; surabhi — fragrant; madhuraiḥ — sweet; kalpa — wish-fulfilling; vallyaḥ — creepers; samantāt — on every side; cakruḥ — performed; nīrājanam — the rite of nīrājana; iva — as it were; muhuḥ — again and again; kūjitaiḥ — with the singing; kokilānām — of cuckoos; saṅkurvatyaḥ — raising; jaya jaya jaya — victory, victory, victory; iti — thus; uccakaiḥ — loudly; harṣa — of joy; nādam — a cry.

95Then, as the lovely young women went up [into the pavilion], the wish-fulfilling creepers grown within it on every side performed, as it were, nīrājana over them with various fragrant, sweet flowers, and with the singing of the cuckoos again and again loudly raised a joyful cry: "Victory, victory, victory!"

Note. The metre is mandākrāntā. Nīrājana is a rite of welcome: a lamp, flowers and the like are waved before one who is honoured.

Colophon: iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye navamaḥ sargaḥ — "Thus [ends] the ninth sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'." (The colophon gives no title for the sarga.)
